claims.text: The target material is equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Applying a thin oxidation-resistant coating to equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr will improve its high-temperature oxygen resistance.
The coating will act as a barrier against oxygen penetration.
The coating will preserve the mechanical properties of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate oxygen resistance that limits high-temperature applications.
The proposed protection applies during exposure to air at 800 °C for 5 h.
The proposed protection applies under loading at strain rates from 10^-4 to 10^-2 s^-1.
The coating's effectiveness above 800 °C is uncertain.
The coating's long-term durability is uncertain.
Coated and uncoated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr specimens can be compared after exposure to air at 800 °C for 5 h using weight gain, surface oxidation, and microstructural analysis.
The hypothesis is falsified if the coated specimen shows no significant improvement in oxygen resistance over the uncoated specimen.

contradictions.description: The conditions claim applicability to long-term exposure, but the defined exposure is only 5 h and long-term coating durability is explicitly stated to be uncertain.
